test.title: Learning an instrument as an adult

paragraphs.text: Many adults take up a musical instrument, but opinions differ about what helps them succeed. Music teacher Olga Petrova believes adults should practise for short periods every day rather than for hours at the weekend, because regular practice builds memory more effectively.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Psychologist Daniel Frost studies motivation. His research suggests that adults who join a group or band are three times more likely to continue playing after a year than those who learn alone, mainly because they do not want to let others down.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Composer Amira Haddad argues that adults are often held back by the belief that they are too old to improve. She encourages her students to record themselves each month, so that they can hear their own progress.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Petrova and Haddad both warn against choosing music that is too difficult too early. Frost adds that choosing an instrument that fits a person’s lifestyle, such as one that is easy to carry, also affects whether people continue.
paragraphs.label: D
